evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the idealized full-range Hooke-law assumption rather than add an unrelated process. The parent says that at fixed mass and damping, changing initial displacement only scales the sampled x values along one line in the dv_dt-versus-(x,v) relation; the restoring slope with respect to x is constant. The child would make that slope depend on amplitude, so when comparing trajectories started with small versus larger displacement but similar velocity range, the acceleration becomes disproportionately more restoring at larger |x|. This changes the scored target mapping directly because dv_dt as a function of observed x and v is altered, not merely an auxiliary trajectory. The effect is admissible in passive one-dimensional motion, preserves continuity and sign-reversal symmetry, and remains energy-dissipative because the damping law is unchanged and no drive is introduced. The limitation is that if all observed displacements stay very small, the refinement is practically unidentifiable and the parent is recovered.

change_summary: The support is no longer assumed to equilibrate instantaneously; instead, its effective deformation relaxes with a finite time constant before generating the linear-plus-cubic restoring load. assumption_audit.mechanism: Standard linear solid/anelastic support relaxation: part of the elastic load is carried by an internal strain-like degree of freedom that relaxes toward the current displacement over finite time, creating passive rate-dependent stiffness.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: In the fast-relaxation limit relaxation_time -> 0, the internal state satisfies z -> x quasi-instantly and the successor reduces to the parent restoring law.

response_change.parent_relation: The restoring force is an instantaneous odd function of displacement only: for fixed parameters, dv_dt versus x at a given v has a single time-invariant cubic-shaped curve.
